labeling_corrections: OpenRouter cached reported latency is assumed to be TTFT/base time; it is not verified TTFT.
8B cached model-level series lacks a historical provider label; Alibaba attribution is inferred from the current sole endpoint.
limitations: These are distinct what-if scenarios, not confidence intervals, hard bounds or measured provider latency.
Published cached latency labels may themselves be ambiguous. Profiles preserve whether reported latency is only assumed to be TTFT/per-call base; this is separate from throughput ambiguity.
TTFT includes unmatched prefill/network/queue work. No extra prefill-token/rate charge is added and no prefill scaling slope is inferred.
EOS termination, forced-closure prefill latency and within-call host work are not separately modeled. The forced phase protocol assumes custom server support.
Measured outer host overhead stays local. Provider model/checkpoint/precision/template/sampling changes can alter quality and trajectories; observed local accuracy is held fixed, not transferred.

Profile routing checks the explicit model family and recorded checkpoint basename. The native 122B checkpoint is a local 5-bit conversion; family matching does not establish provider precision or execution equivalence.
Native and prior screens use different prompts/controllers and are summarized separately. Original KV-relay experiments and posthoc final ablations are unsupported/excluded.
verified: All saved source code, result ledgers, manifests, summary ledgers and pinned question/corpus inputs verified by extractor.
Per-call counts reconcile row totals; sampled EOS and forced input controls are separate from generated tokens.
Profile model family and actual local checkpoint basename must match the declared screen.
All source snapshots are confined and SHA256-verified; no source body is embedded.
All408 projected conditions retain exact saved predictions and scores.
All17 paired comparisons contain identical12 question IDs.
All6 Lambda profiles emit only the known-TPOT decode scenario.
